logline: A young woman partially taken over by an alien parasite becomes an uneasy ally to a government task force hunting the beings that have infiltrated human society.

renewal.note: Netflix classified as a limited series; no Season 2 renewal. Director Yeon Sang-ho has noted story could continue but Netflix has not greenlit a follow-up.

bollymeter.basis: 100% Rotten Tomatoes from 14 critics and a #1 Netflix non-English slot in 68 countries signal a genuinely accomplished adaptation; IMDb audience landing at 7.1 reflects the genre limitations and underexplored thematic depth critics also flagged.

pull_quotes.text: As a horror series, Parasyte: The Grey is superb. As sci-fi, it's exciting. As an adaptation, this is a showstopper.

seasons.review_body: Director Yeon Sang-ho (Train to Busan) brings the Japanese Parasyte manga into Korean live-action with full genre commitment: the body-horror transformation sequences are practical and unsettling, Jeon So-nee's lead performance is physically demanding and emotionally grounded, and the six-episode runtime is lean enough to keep momentum. Critics were markedly generous: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 14 reviewers, and the show topped Netflix's global non-English chart in 68 countries its first week with 31.5 million hours watched. The minority critique, shared by both Jonathan Wilson at Ready Steady Cut and the IMDb audience score of 7.1, is that the themes remain surface-level and the sci-fi world-building is subordinated to action set-pieces. A Parasite manga purist cameo at the finale gives the story a clear continuation hook that Netflix has, as yet, declined to pursue.
